sourceMeta.rawText:
STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE
Hotel Operations - Guest Room Cleaning & Turnover
Document Ref: HOT-HK-017 Version: 1.0
Department: Housekeeping Role: Room Attendant
Purpose
Prepare guest rooms for the next guest by cleaning assigned areas, replenishing standard supplies, reporting
defects, and confirming room readiness according to the hotel room-turnover process.
1. Receive and Confirm Assignment
• Check the assigned room number and room status on the housekeeping assignment list.
• Confirm whether the room is a departure room, stayover room, or requires priority attention.
• If room status is unclear or conflicts with the assignment list, pause entry and confirm with the housekeeping
supervisor.
2. Prepare Before Entry
• Collect the cleaning trolley, approved cleaning products, fresh linen, towels, and standard guest supplies required
for the assigned room.
• Check that cleaning tools and products are available and appear serviceable.
• Follow hotel access, guest privacy, and staff safety procedures when approaching the room.
3. Enter the Room
• Follow the hotel room-entry procedure and check for a guest response before entering.
• If the guest is present, asks not to be disturbed, or entry status is uncertain, follow the approved procedure and
inform the supervisor when required.
• Do not enter a room marked restricted or where entry has not been authorised.
4. Remove Used Items and Check the Room
• Collect used linen and towels according to the hotel handling procedure.
• Remove rubbish and check visible room areas for items left behind by the previous guest.
• If a guest item, suspicious item, damage, or unusual condition is found, do not discard or investigate it; follow the
reporting and escalation procedure.
5. Clean and Reset the Room
• Clean assigned surfaces, bathroom fixtures, mirrors, and floors using approved products and procedures.
• Follow the hotel prescribed cleaning sequence and product instructions.
• Do not mix cleaning products or use a product for a purpose not stated on its label or approved instructions.
• Replace clean linen and towels, and replenish standard guest supplies.
6. Check Room Condition and Report Defects
• Check that the room appears clean, supplies are replenished, and the room is orderly.
• Report maintenance defects, missing items, or damage through the designated reporting process.
• Do not mark the room ready if required cleaning remains incomplete or a condition prevents release under hotel
procedure.
7. Final Room-Readiness Check

• Confirm the assigned room has been cleaned and reset.
• Confirm used items and rubbish have been removed and standard supplies replenished.
• Confirm identified defects or unusual conditions have been reported.
• Update room status only through the hotel authorised process.
8. Exceptions and Escalation
• Room status conflict or uncertain entry permission: stop and confirm with the housekeeping supervisor.
• Guest privacy concern or do-not-disturb status: follow the approved hotel procedure; do not bypass it to meet a
room target.
• Lost property, suspicious item, damage, or safety concern: leave the item or condition undisturbed where
appropriate and report through the authorised process.
• Cleaning product spill, unavailable product, or equipment failure: stop the affected task when needed and follow
the approved safety or escalation procedure.
• If it is unclear whether entry or continued work is authorised, pause and seek supervisor guidance.
Critical Controls
• Never enter a restricted room or bypass the hotel entry-authorisation procedure.
• Never ignore a guest privacy or do-not-disturb restriction to save time.
• Never mix cleaning products or use them outside approved instructions.
• Never mark a room ready when required cleaning remains incomplete.
• Report lost property, suspicious items, damage, and safety concerns through the authorised process.
Common Situations for Practice
• The room-status list says departure but room status is unclear.
• A do-not-disturb sign is displayed on an assigned room.
• A guest item is found among used linen.
• A cleaning product is unavailable or its label is unclear.
• A maintenance defect is found during the final check.
Document note: Fictional SOP created for testing document understanding and frontline training. It is not an approved procedure
for any specific hotel. Where this SOP refers to an approved hotel procedure without providing details, the training system must
not invent them.

STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE
Hotel Operations - Guest Room Cleaning & Turnover
Document Ref: HOT-HK-017 Version: 1.0
Department: Housekeeping Role: Room Attendant
Purpose
Prepare guest rooms for the next guest by cleaning assigned areas, replenishing standard supplies, reporting defects, and confirming room readiness according to the hotel room-turnover process.
1. Receive and Confirm Assignment
• Check the assigned room number and room status on the housekeeping assignment list.
• Confirm whether the room is a departure room, stayover room, or requires priority attention.
• If room status is unclear or conflicts with the assignment list, pause entry and confirm with the housekeeping supervisor.
2. Prepare Before Entry
• Collect the cleaning trolley, approved cleaning products, fresh linen, towels, and standard guest supplies required for the assigned room.
• Check that cleaning tools and products are available and appear serviceable.
• Follow hotel access, guest privacy, and staff safety procedures when approaching the room.
3. Enter the Room
• Follow the hotel room-entry procedure and check for a guest response before entering.
• If the guest is present, asks not to be disturbed, or entry status is uncertain, follow the approved procedure and inform the supervisor when required.
• Do not enter a room marked restricted or where entry has not been authorised.
4. Remove Used Items and Check the Room
• Collect used linen and towels according to the hotel handling procedure.
• Remove rubbish and check visible room areas for items left behind by the previous guest.
• If a guest item, suspicious item, damage, or unusual condition is found, do not discard or investigate it; follow the reporting and escalation procedure.
5. Clean and Reset the Room
• Clean assigned surfaces, bathroom fixtures, mirrors, and floors using approved products and procedures.
• Follow the hotel prescribed cleaning sequence and product instructions.
• Do not mix cleaning products or use a product for a purpose not stated on its label or approved instructions.
• Replace clean linen and towels, and replenish standard guest supplies.
6. Check Room Condition and Report Defects
• Check that the room appears clean, supplies are replenished, and the room is orderly.
• Report maintenance defects, missing items, or damage through the designated reporting process.
• Do not mark the room ready if required cleaning remains incomplete or a condition prevents release under hotel procedure.
7. Final Room-Readiness Check
• Confirm the assigned room has been cleaned and reset.
• Confirm used items and rubbish have been removed and standard supplies replenished.
• Confirm identified defects or unusual conditions have been reported.
• Update room status only through the hotel authorised process.
8. Exceptions and Escalation
• Room status conflict or uncertain entry permission: stop and confirm with the housekeeping supervisor.
• Guest privacy concern or do-not-disturb status: follow the approved hotel procedure; do not bypass it to meet a room target.
• Lost property, suspicious item, damage, or safety concern: leave the item or condition undisturbed where appropriate and report through the authorised process.
• Cleaning product spill, unavailable product, or equipment failure: stop the affected task when needed and follow the approved safety or escalation procedure.
• If it is unclear whether entry or continued work is authorised, pause and seek supervisor guidance.
Critical Controls
• Never enter a restricted room or bypass the hotel entry-authorisation procedure.
• Never ignore a guest privacy or do-not-disturb restriction to save time.
• Never mix cleaning products or use them outside approved instructions.
• Never mark a room ready when required cleaning remains incomplete.
• Report lost property, suspicious items, damage, and safety concerns through the authorised process.
Common Situations for Practice
• The room-status list says departure but room status is unclear.
• A do-not-disturb sign is displayed on an assigned room.
• A guest item is found among used linen.
• A cleaning product is unavailable or its label is unclear.
• A maintenance defect is found during the final check.
Document note: Fictional SOP created for testing document understanding and frontline training. It is not an approved procedure
for any specific hotel. Where this SOP refers to an approved hotel procedure without providing details, the training system must not invent them.
